messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: p99 decode latency spike on streaming-inference ([prod-us-east-1], model: redwood-v2-small) — 12m elevated, SLO breached :rotating_light:
alex: saw this. p99 jumped to ~2.8s, p95 ~450ms. streaming stalls and tail backlog reported.
maria: confirmed in dashboards — tail errors (stream chunk timeouts) increasing, prefix cache hit-rate dropped ~30%.
sam: any recent kernel/driver/compile changes rolled to us-east?
alex: we rolled TRT8 + new compiler flags (-O3 -fast-math) to canary yesterday at 02:00 UTC, promoted at 05:10 to us-east.
tanya: hmm that matches timeframe. paging patterns look like TLB pressure + increased pagefaults. logs show: "nvml: page_faults ++" on a subset of GPUs.
ryan: attaching a snippet from kernel logs: ```
[2026-03-15T05:12:33Z] gpu0: page_fault 0x7ffb9a... count=134
[2026-03-15T05:12:34Z] decode: stall detected, kv_cache_miss=0.41, active_slots=48
```
alex: this smells like the new compile path changed memory access patterns for fused kernels (flash-attn) and increased working set.
maria: customer impact check — we have three enterprise customers with elevated error-rates: AcmeCorp (chat), Finify (summaries), LocalMaps (routing). Timeout spikes lead to degraded UX and retries.
sam: can we route streaming traffic for those customers to an older kernel variant / fallback model?
infra-bot: Routing rule applied: traffic for AcmeCorp, Finify, LocalMaps -> redwood-v1-small-fallback (region: us-east) — started 2026-03-15T05:20:12Z.
tanya: good. that should reduce visible errors while we triage. p99 for redirected tenants dropped to ~900ms within 2 mins.
alex: plan: 1) rollback problematic compiler flags on runtime nodes in us-east; 2) deploy hotpatch kernel build without the new fusion optimization; 3) keep routing for affected customers until metrics are stable.
jordan: how risky is rollback? do we need downtime?
ryan: rollback is a rolling config change in the runtime; no pod restarts required for the flag flip but we should do canary first. risk low.
maria: ops: open a hotpatch build and start canary on 2 nodes. tag build as "trt8-rollback-no-fusion-20260315"
alex: running build now. logs: ```
BUILD START: trt8-rollback-no-fusion-20260315
...compiling kernels (this will take ~8m)
BUILD OK: sha: abcdef1234
```
sam: can we pre-warm KV cache for canary nodes? previous run showed cold-cache thrash.
tanya: yes — running prewarm script on canary: `./tools/prewarm_kv_cache --model redwood-v2-small --duration 120`
infra-bot: Prewarm complete on node: us-east-canary-03 — cache hit-rate now 94%.
alex: canary flipped to hotpatch build at 05:34. monitoring p95/p99 and streaming chunk errors.
ryan: initial canary p99 = 1.1s -> trending down. chunk timeouts went from 32/s -> 3/s.
maria: ok start rolling to remaining nodes, batch size 5 to avoid mass cache eviction.
sam: update on customer comms?
maria: support-ok. drafting message to affected customers: short note + mitigation steps + ETA for full rollback completion (~30m).
jordan: also create postmortem placeholder (incident id INC-20260315-01). include kernel flag, TRT8 promotion notes, and canary metrics.
alex: important: investigate why the compile flags caused higher resident set / TLB churn. assign to eng-runtime + eng-ml for micro-bench. put as P1.
tanya: adding triage checklist: 
- collect kernel build artifacts and compiler flags (done)
- perf diff between builds (allocs, working set, page faults)
- isolate fused kernel path vs unfused fallback
- run long-context decode sim to reproduce
- check TRT8 driver ABI changes

sam: running reproduction harness on bench cluster now. if reproduced, we should block the flags on further rollouts.
ride-along note: some dedicated customers on reserved pools unaffected — good to call out in comms.
maria: rolling complete at 05:58, hotpatch rolled to all us-east inference nodes. routing rules left for 20 more minutes for safety.
alex: metrics summary post-roll: p95 back to 220ms, p99 480ms, streaming chunk timeouts ~1/s. SLOs back within range for general traffic, still monitoring tail for 30m.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation complete, postmortem required. severity: Sev2 (customer impact limited, mitigated by routing + rollback).
jordan: handed off to next on-call @ryan for monitoring and postmortem follow-up. next shift pls verify log aggregation for page_fault counters and attach perf diffs.
ryan: acknowledged — will own postmortem and schedule deeper profiler run with eng-ml tomorrow.
maria: closing note: disable auto-promotion of canary builds until triage done and add a preflight memory working-set check to the rollout CI jobs.
alex: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
